text: Patient Information Test Results Results are part of your ongoing care and should be reviewed with a doctor who can explain what they mean in context. Information for patients of Woolloongabba Medical Centre in Brisbane’s inner south. Need help with a result? Book a follow-up or call reception for administrative assistance. Book Follow-up Call Clinic How results are managed Our current policy is that test results are discussed with a doctor so they can be interpreted in the context of your health and the reason the test was requested. If your usual doctor is unavailable, another doctor practising at the clinic can review the result with you. Results are not simply administrative information; they may need interpretation alongside your symptoms, history, medications and the reason the test was requested. Patient communications We use HotDoc to help us reach you. Woolloongabba Medical Centre uses HotDoc as a patient communication partner. Depending on the clinical context and our current settings, you may receive a secure health or result message by SMS or email that asks you to verify your details before viewing the message or booking follow-up care. A HotDoc message does not replace clinical review. If your doctor asked you to return, or you are worried about a result or your symptoms, book the recommended follow-up or contact the clinic. Follow-up Book a follow-up appointment after your test when your doctor has advised review is required, or whenever you are uncertain about the result or next step. We also use recall and reminder systems to support preventive and follow-up care. Please keep your phone number, email and address current so the team can contact you when needed. Significant or urgent findings If a result requires prompt clinical attention, we may contact you using the details held in your record. The absence of a call should not be taken as confirmation that a result is normal or requires no follow-up. Your responsibility If you were asked to return for results, please make the follow-up appointment even if we have not contacted you. Recall and reminder system We use a recall and reminder system to support preventive care and follow-up. From time to time the team may contact you about care that is appropriate for you. Please keep your contact details current and discuss any questions about reminders with your doctor. The current appointment guide lists a simple results follow-up as a standard consultation. Test result questions How do I receive my test results? Our current policy is that test results are discussed with a doctor so the result can be interpreted in the context of your health and the reason the test was requested. Should I book follow-up if I have not been contacted? If your doctor asked you to return for results, make the follow-up appointment even if we have not contacted you. Book an appointment → Do you use recalls and reminders? Yes. We use recall and reminder systems to support preventive and follow-up care. title: Pathology
description: Information about independent on-site pathology collection, including referrals, preparation, results and provider fees.
headings: How to access the service and prepare.
Know who is responsible for fees.
Patient guides for this area of care.
text: Independent On-Site Service Pathology Patients can access pathology collection on site through an independent third-party provider. The pathology service is not owned or operated by Woolloongabba Medical Centre. Service information Accessing pathology services. Pathology testing examines samples such as blood, urine, swabs or other specimens to help diagnose, screen for or monitor health conditions. Your GP or another authorised clinician may provide a pathology request when testing is clinically appropriate. The tests collected, collection requirements and laboratory processing are controlled by the independent pathology provider. Independent provider. This service is provided by a separate third-party business and is not owned or operated by Woolloongabba Medical Centre. Provider availability, opening hours, service scope, fees and billing can change independently of the medical centre. Before you attend How to access the service and prepare. How to access pathology Bring the pathology request form or electronic request details provided by your clinician. Many routine collections may not require an appointment, but some tests need a specific booking or collection time. Confirm this with the pathology provider. Before collection Follow the instructions provided for your test. Some tests require fasting, timed collection, medication instructions or other preparation. Bring your Medicare card and any information requested by the pathology provider. After the service Results, medicines and follow-up. Results are generally sent to the clinician who requested the test. Arrange follow-up with the requesting clinician as advised so results can be interpreted in the context of your health and treatment plan. Do not rely on a laboratory result alone to make changes to medicines or treatment unless a clinician has advised you to do so. Costs Know who is responsible for fees. Third-party provider fees are separate. Pathology charges are set and billed by the independent pathology provider. Many clinically indicated pathology tests are Medicare funded, but not every test or circumstance is covered. Ask the provider about any fee before collection if you are unsure. A GP consultation at Woolloongabba Medical Centre is billed separately under the medical centre billing policy. Read Woolloongabba Medical Centre Fees & Billing Patient questions Frequently Asked Questions Do I need a pathology request? Most pathology testing requires a request from an authorised clinician. Bring the request details with you and check with the provider if you are unsure. Do I need to fast? Only some tests require fasting or other preparation. Follow the instructions from your clinician or pathology provider rather than fasting unless you have been told to do so. Who gives me my results? The clinician who requested the test is usually responsible for explaining the result and any next steps. Arrange follow-up as advised. Is the pathology service part of Woolloongabba Medical Centre? No. The on-site pathology service is operated by an independent third-party provider. Its staffing, opening hours, fees and billing are separate from the medical centre.
